title: Step Supporting Observation Unit Behavioral Contract

scope.purpose: Define the observation responsibilities, activity boundary, observation output semantics, provenance, and custody obligations of an optional Step Supporting Observation Unit.
scope.appliesTo: A concrete Step specialization that selects and coordinates one or more Observation Unit instances.

definition.observationUnitInstance: One concrete runtime instance identified by observationUnitIdentity.
definition.observationActivity: One distinct authorized activity identified by observationInvocationIdentity. A specialization may realize it as a call, callback, subscription activation, sampling cycle, or another explicit mechanism.
definition.observationRecord: One independently identifiable fact, measurement, event, or diagnostic observation identified by observationRecordIdentity.
definition.observationSubject: The entity, operation, execution fact, or scope about which an observation is made. It may be distinct from the association target.
definition.observationContext: The target/source context and correlation information required to interpret an observation.
definition.observationDestination: The explicitly defined recipient to which an observation record is emitted. It is not assumed to be a central collector.

optionality: A Step is not required to select, provision, associate, or activate any Observation Unit.
The framework does not make observation mandatory for every Step.
Each Step selects only the observation capabilities required by its responsibility.
observationSemantics: An Observation Unit observes, measures, captures, or records facts within its specialized capability.
An observation is not a validation judgment, business approval, error classification, or Step flow decision.
The concrete Observation Unit specialization defines what it observes and the semantics and structure of its observation payload.
Step Composition defines observation intent, timing, trigger, correlation context, and Step-specific use of emitted observations.
separation: Observation output is independent of SPUExecutionResult, StepValidatorResult, ErrorResult, ErrorHandlerResult, and StepExecutionResult.

Observation events, logs, telemetry, and Observation Unit results remain outside the common StepExecutionResult contract unless a concrete Step defines a separate explicit application-specific integration.
Observation output does not imply that the observed operation succeeded or failed.
identity: observationUnitIdentity, observationUnitAssociationIdentity, associationTargetIdentity, stepInstanceIdentity, observationInvocationIdentity, and observationRecordIdentity identify distinct facts.
Each observation activity is correlated with exactly one association context when performed under an association.
Every separately identifiable emitted record has its own observationRecordIdentity, including multiple records from one activity.

behavioralContract.capability: Observe or measure explicitly scoped facts and emit observation records through a specialization-defined mechanism, preserving provenance.
responsibilities: Perform the observation, measurement, capture, or recording capability defined by the concrete specialization.
Use the observation input and context supplied or made accessible through the authorized observation boundary.
Preserve the distinction between the observed fact and any interpretation or decision made by Step Composition or another consumer.
Produce records whose provenance identifies the producing instance, activity, association, target scope, and owning Step.
Deliver records through the destination and handoff mechanism defined by the specialization.
Report inability to perform or complete observation through the declared failure boundary without fabricating records.
Preserve each produced record until the defined handoff/acceptance point.
nonResponsibilities: Selecting, creating, changing, rebinding, or ending associations.
Provisioning, admitting, retaining, quiescing, or releasing the instance.
Deciding observation intent, business meaning, trigger policy, or Step flow topology.
Making validation judgments or deciding whether an observed condition is acceptable.
Creating SPUError or StepError occurrences merely because an observed fact is noteworthy.
Choosing Step transitions, retries, continuation, compensation, or termination.
Constructing or mutating SPUExecutionResult, StepValidatorResult, ErrorResult, ErrorHandlerResult, or StepExecutionResult.
Requiring a central telemetry service, event bus, logger, database, or global observation manager.

observationActivityBoundary.authority: Step Composition authorizes and coordinates observation activity within the owning Step.
observationActivityBoundary.conceptualActivity: ObservationActivity consists of one observationInvocationIdentity, one authorized association context, observation input, and specialization-defined observation context.
implementationFreedom: No separately allocated request object, universal method name, or callable signature is mandated.
A specialization may use explicit calls, callbacks, event-driven capture, sampling, subscriptions, or another defined mechanism.
Observation may be synchronous, asynchronous, incremental, or completion-based as defined by the specialization.
The mechanism must preserve identity, association, provenance, and custody obligations.
specializationDefinedInformation: observationInput: optional event, measurement request, instruction, or data required by the capability.
observationContext: target/source context and correlation information required to interpret facts.
observation configuration, filters, sampling parameters, or measurement options where applicable.
A target snapshot, immutable view, borrowed reference, handle, callback, or subscription source where required.
A destination identity or delivery capability when output is externally emitted.
bindingRules: Step Composition selects an association valid for the instance and intended target before authorizing activity.
Each activity is bound to exactly one observationUnitAssociationIdentity and its corresponding associationTargetIdentity.
If one instance has multiple associations, the selected association must be explicit; the Unit must not infer or substitute another target.
An authorized activity must not be silently redirected if the association changes while the activity is in progress.
The concrete Step defines whether the observed target is a snapshot, live context, event source, or subscription and defines freshness/consistency guarantees.

observationRecordContract.producer: The Observation Unit instance or a specialization-defined capture mechanism operating under its identity.
observationRecordContract.meaning: One independently identifiable fact, measurement, event, or diagnostic observation.
observationRecordContract.payload: TObservationPayload is defined by the concrete specialization and may represent a measurement, event fact, sampled value, timing datum, state snapshot, or other observation content.
optionalMetadata: observationSubjectIdentity when the subject differs from the association target.
observationTimestamp or monotonic measurement time where relevant.
sourceInvocationIdentity or sourceEventIdentity when correlating with a distinct SPU/Step activity.
Sequence/order metadata where required by the emission mechanism.
Specialization-defined quality, precision, units, sampling, or diagnostic metadata.
semantics: One observation activity may emit zero, one, or multiple records.
A record describes an observation; it does not assert a validation verdict or prescribe a response.
No universal event schema, timestamp format, measurement unit, severity, or payload representation is imposed.
Record provenance remains stable after association dissociation or instance release.
Two records with identical payloads remain distinct when their record identities differ.

outputAndCustody.cardinality: Zero or more records may be emitted by one activity. An optional activity-completion indication may be produced where required.
productionOwnership: The Observation Unit owns the observation operation and construction of records it produces.
The Unit preserves each produced record until accepted by its declared destination or explicitly transferred to a recovery owner.
Delivery attempt alone does not establish acceptance when the mechanism can reject or leave acceptance indeterminate.
handoff: The specialization defines the destination and exact acceptance point.
The destination may be Step Composition, a Step-owned observation consumer, or an explicitly selected external destination; no central sink is mandated.
Upon acceptance, custody follows the destination contract. Step Composition retains records only where the concrete Step assigns that custody to it.
Rejected or indeterminate acceptance requires specialization-defined reconciliation and recovery to prevent silent loss or duplicate delivery.
For incremental emission, each record's identity and custody status must be independently correlatable.
completion: Activity completion is distinct from production of individual records.
An activity may complete normally while emitting zero records.
Records accepted before a later exception remain valid and must not be revoked or rewritten.
The specialization defines reconciliation of pending, in-flight, or partially emitted records on abnormal completion or cancellation.

failureAndExceptionBoundary.principle: Observed facts, delivery outcomes, and failures of the observation mechanism are distinct.
rules: A noteworthy or negative observed fact is not automatically an Observation Unit failure or error occurrence.
Failure to access a source, measure a value, construct a record, or deliver it is classified by the concrete specialization.
An exception does not fabricate an Observation Record.
An exception after records have been accepted does not revoke those records.
No universal exception taxonomy, retry policy, severity, or conversion into SPUError/StepError is prescribed.
Step Composition decides how an observation failure affects its flow, if at all.

stepComposition: Defines observation intent, trigger, timing, ordering, correlation, and execution mode for the concrete Step.
Selects the association and target context, coordinates activation, and supplies required input/context.
Determines whether it or another destination accepts custody of observation records.
Determines how observation output is consumed, retained, forwarded, or correlated with Step execution evidence.
Applies the concrete Step's response policy to observation failures.
observationUnit: Executes the specialized observation capability and emits factual observation records.
Does not decide the business meaning or acceptability of observed facts.
Does not choose Step flow transitions or assemble Step results.
responsibilityBoundary.stepResultBoundary: Observation Records and activity-completion information remain independent of StepExecutionResult. A concrete Step may define an explicit application-specific integration, but observation data is not a default StepExecutionResult field.

retentionAndHistoricalInterpretation.principle: Observation records may outlive the association and Observation Unit instance that produced them.
rules: The concrete Step or destination defines retention duration, representation, access policy, and deletion conditions.
Retained records preserve required provenance for as long as they remain observable or referenced.
An ended association remains historical provenance but cannot authorize new activities.
A released instance may remain referenced by historical identity without remaining callable.
Record content must remain interpretable without the original runtime instance unless an explicit independent dependency is defined.

required: Define the facts, events, measurements, or diagnostics the Unit can observe.
Define the subject and target-context model and its correspondence to associationTargetIdentity.
Define the activity mechanism: call, callback, event, sampling, subscription, or another explicit model.
Define concrete observation input/configuration types where applicable.
Define Observation Record payload, metadata, and required provenance.
Define identity generation and uniqueness scope for observationInvocationIdentity and observationRecordIdentity.
Define zero/multiple record semantics and ordering guarantees.
Define destination, handoff/acceptance point, custody, and recovery behavior.
Define completion, cancellation, partial emission, and failure behavior.
Define synchronous/asynchronous execution, concurrency, reentrancy, buffering, and backpressure where applicable.
Define record retention and detachment requirements.
Define how Step Composition coordinates and consumes observations without conflating them with validation, error, processing, or Step result contracts.
specializationRequirements.completionRule: A specialization is complete when its capability, activity mechanism, target/association binding, record semantics, provenance, destination, custody, lifecycle interaction, and applicable failure/concurrency behavior are explicit.

explicitNonGoals: No mandatory Observation Unit for every Step or SPU.
No universal execute signature or mandatory request/response object.
No universal event schema, timestamp format, measurement unit, severity, or telemetry protocol.
No mandatory central logger, event bus, broker, database, collector, or observation manager.
No validation verdict, business approval, error classification, or Step flow-control authority.
No association or lifecycle management authority for the Observation Unit.
No default inclusion of observation records in StepExecutionResult.
No universal synchronous, asynchronous, periodic, streaming, or subscription model.

references.relationship: Association identity, target binding, applicability, validity, and dissociation.
Instance readiness, activation eligibility, quiescence, reuse, and release.
Step Composition authority over observation coordination, internal flow, and supporting-unit lifecycle.
Owning Step boundary and optional supporting-unit selection.
SPU invocation context and possible observation subject.
Explicit exclusion of observability events, logs, telemetry, and Observation Unit results from the common Step result.
Observation Unit independent observation semantics/results and Step Composition coordination.

openDesignDetails: Define concrete observation payload schemas and event/measurement semantics per Step specialization.
Define the selected observation destination and its delivery/acceptance protocol.
Define ordering, timestamp source, sampling precision, buffering, and backpressure guarantees where required.
Define concrete association scopes and instance lifecycle behavior for each Observation Unit specialization.
